top.title: Former Barcelona forward urges patience with Real Madrid’s South American stars
top.description: Former Barcelona forward urges patience with Real Madrid’s South American stars Vitor Roque has been enjoying life ever since his return to Brazil. Since joining Palmeiras in 2025, the forward has racked up 29 goals, and his market value has also gone up. This comes on the back of a disastrous spell at Barcelona, where the player struggled to prove himself and eventually left the club permanently in 2025. In light of his success, the former Barcelona forward was recently asked about the lack of patience from European clubs when it comes to talents from South America. Vitor Roque on Endrick and Mastantuono Roque believes players like Endrick need more time. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) When asked about the South American talents, the interviewer particularly referenced two Real Madrid players: Endrick and Franco Mastantuono. Both players had joined Real Madrid in the recent past. While Mastantuono had to settle for a loan at Fiorentina, Endrick is also struggling with a lack of game time despite being a part of Jose Mourinho’s setup this season. Keeping that in mind, Roque urged more patience with these players. “People believe that young people arrive and we have to start playing 100%, giving everything, doing our best football, but it is not. It takes patience. Sometimes we don’t have the adaptation time we need,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). The former Barcelona forward pointed out how language and culture can also be a problem for young South American stars. “We are very young and speaking a new language is very difficult. Sometimes it is important to have the support of the coach and I when I went to Barcelona I did not have it. They barely talked to me, you know? “So I think you have to keep that in mind and a lot of people don’t see it that way, they think you have to be prepared from the first minute ,” he added. What’s next for Endrick and Mastantuono? Mastantuono’s fate will be decided at the end of the season. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Fortunately, it appears Real Madrid are ready to bide their time with both Endrick and Mastantuono. Especially in the case of Endrick, the club have not shown any indication of permanently parting ways with the forward. They are, in fact, ready to block a January exit for the Brazilian international, who is rated highly by coach Mourinho. As for Mastantuono, the Argentine has shown glimpses of his talents at Fiorentina. But unless he breaks out in a big way like Nico Paz, it is unlikely Real Madrid will want to make him a part of the first-team setup next season.

top.title: 2027: APC, APGA stakeholders unite for Tinubu’s re-election in Anambra
top.description: Stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) in Orumba South Local Government Area of Anambra State have agreed to work together to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. The stakeholders also pledged to support Governor Chukwuma Charles Soludo’s position backing Tinubu’s second-term ambition. The resolution was reached at a joint stakeholders’ meeting held on Saturday, November 28, 2026, and convened by the Chairman of Orumba South Local Government, Hon. Shedrack Azubuike, in collaboration with Booth 2 Booth with Bola Tinubu, an APC support group led by its National Coordinator, Mr Ikechukwu Madu. At the meeting, the stakeholders agreed to strengthen political cooperation, unity and mutual understanding between the two parties, stressing the importance of working across party lines in pursuit of shared political and developmental interests. A major outcome of the meeting was the decision to support Soludo’s position on Tinubu’s re-election and mobilise grassroots support across Orumba South. To achieve this, the stakeholders resolved to establish a joint APC–APGA mobilisation committee to coordinate political engagement and grassroots mobilisation across the 18 wards of the local government area. They also agreed to promote peaceful political coexistence, political tolerance and constructive engagement, while sustaining regular consultations and collaborative initiatives for the development of Orumba South. The stakeholders commended Azubuike and Madu for initiating the engagement, describing the meeting as an opportunity to strengthen cooperation among political stakeholders and establish a common platform around shared objectives. Those present included the Deputy National Coordinator of Booth 2 Booth, Mr Jafar Abdulahi Ibrahim; the group’s Anambra State Coordinator, Mr Paschal Candle; and the APC Anambra State Organising Secretary, Mr Izuchukwu Okeke. The meeting ended with a reaffirmation of the stakeholders’ commitment to sustained APC–APGA cooperation, support for Soludo’s position on Tinubu’s re-election and grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. top.title: Atlético beat Viking 2-0 as both strikers score, but Sørloth injury hits Barcelona trip
top.description: Atlético beat Viking 2-0 as both strikers score, but Sørloth injury hits Barcelona trip Alexander Sørloth and Julián Álvarez both ended goal droughts as Atlético Madrid beat Viking FK 2-0 to reach seven points in the Champions League. Sørloth's muscle injury now adds to an injury list that already includes Lookman, just as Atlético face Barcelona and PSV. Atlético Madrid’s win over Viking FK revived their hopes of a direct top-eight finish. Three league-phase games remain, and one of them is away to PSV. Both of Simeone’s leading strikers found the net. Yet the night also added a new name to the injury list. Sørloth broke the deadlock by firing in a pass from Alejandro Grimaldo. Five minutes later, Álvarez’s free-kick crept in at the near post. It was his 27th goal in the Champions League. It was also his first Champions League goal at the Metropolitano in 210 days. The strike was his third of the 2026-27 season: one in LaLiga and two in Europe. Grimaldo was named Player of the Match. Viking defender Henrik Falchener was sent off late in the game. Win steadies a European campaign that stalled against Bayern The result follows an uneven league phase. Atlético opened with a 2-1 defeat at Liverpool. They then beat Manchester United 2-0 at home. A 1-1 draw at Stuttgart followed. Bayern München then won 0-2 at the Metropolitano on 3 November. That home defeat was unusual. Before kick-off against Viking, Atlético had won 11 of their previous 14 home matches in the group stage or league phase. They lost the other three. The victory over the Norwegian side returned them to winning ways in front of their own supporters. The mood inside the stadium was not entirely positive, however. Some home fans whistled Álvarez when he was substituted, even though he had scored. Sørloth injury leaves Simeone short before Barcelona and PSV Sørloth went off limping after 71 minutes. He had taken a heavy knock against the post and left the field with an overload, the club said on 26 November. No date has been set for his return. He will do physiotherapy and gym rehabilitation. The expected absence is significant. ESPN Deportes expects him to miss at least the games against Elche, Barcelona, Real Betis, Valencia and PSV. That would rule him out of the visit to Eindhoven. His injury adds to a list that already includes Lookman. The forward has a high-grade knee sprain. Simeone is therefore short of attacking options for a demanding run of fixtures. The first major test comes at the Spotify Camp Nou on Wednesday 2 December, with kick-off at 20:30 GMT (21:30 in Spain). Viking host Feyenoord on 8 December. Atlético’s next Champions League game follows a day later, away to PSV Eindhoven on 9 December. top.title: ‘He just…’ – Luka Doncic addresses throwing wristband at Spurs fan before post-game altercation
top.description: Photo by Ben Liebenberg/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic found himself in some post-game controversy after the team’s 99-96 loss to the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Cup. Doncic had a mixed night in which he stuffed the box score with 31 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three steals. However, he also took 31 shots, shot 1-13 from three-point range, and left with a high-profile loss to their rivals in San Antonio. As Doncic left the court, he appeared to throw his wristband at some Spurs fans courtside, who did not appreciate the gesture. As Doncic went to pick the wristband back up, a fan shoved him back, leading to a highly contentious postgame moment. Luka Doncic addresses what went down in post-game shove with Spurs fan Doncic spoke to the media after the game and explained what went down, revealing that this is something he does every game, and he got shoved by the fan when he heard them say they didn’t want it and went to retrieve it. “I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn’t want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else.” Anyone who has seen Doncic play in Dallas or Los Angeles knows he does throw his wristbands at fans after the game, usually because they want to take it home with them as memorabilia. Mavericks fan and the lead producer for LeBron James’ ‘Mind the Game’ podcast, Jason Gallagher , revealed that Doncic has done the same towards his child, but in a way that was always considered Doncic being charitable with fans. “He nonchalantly throws wristbands/headbands at fans all the time. My kid has one! Tons of players do that. It sure looks like he didn’t like what this woman said, so he went back and got it from a fan who didn’t want it. Then the dork shoved him lol.” Doncic seemed to aggressively throw the wristband, which went low and hit the woman that the Spurs fan presumably came to the game with, leading to the fan’s aggressive response when Doncic approached them to get the wristband back. The heightened tensions of this early-season marquee clash between Doncic and Victor Wembanyama’s Spurs seemed to have fans on edge, especially as this was a couple in Spurs jerseys who probably did not want Doncic’s wristband anyway, and disagreed with him throwing it towards them. top.title: Thioune concedes Bremen fortunate to draw Gladbach as West Ham loanee Füllkrug discusses potential red card incident
top.description: Thioune concedes Bremen fortunate to draw Gladbach as West Ham loanee Füllkrug discusses potential red card incident With 13 points from their first five Weserstadion encounters, sixth-placed Werder Bremen were the overwhelming favorites against cellar-dwellers Borussia Mönchengladbach on Friday. However, it took two goals after the 85th-minute mark to maintain their unbeaten home record. “Today, we got some entertaining football," Daniel Thioune started his post-match interview with Sky Sports on a positive note. "In the end, you have to be happy if you equalize. Gladbach could have wrapped up the game earlier. “We even had a chance to make it 4-3 at the end, that's crazy. That would have been too much. If you get a point based on your mentality, I'm satisfied." Thioune added regarding Cedric Itten’s missed chance after Niclas Füllkrug's injury-time equalizer. The Germany international extended his lead at the top of the scoring chart with his 11th strike since coming back to Bremen on an initial loan deal. The 33-year-old has 14 goals in all competitions, including scoring in every game at Weserstadion. “I don't think Gladbach quite deserves their position in the table,” Füllkrug praised the opposing team after the match. “The last few games have always been close. They played well against Dortmund, and they played well again today, giving us some problems.” Despite the late turnaround, the ex-BVB man wasn't satisfied with their own performance. “When you play the way we have been, expectations rise for yourself. Of course, I'm disappointed. We were far too sloppy, and lost possession far too often. We left room for improvement there today. We have to be honest about that." Füllkrug was fortunate to repeat his Dortmund heroics because Felix Zwayer could've easily sent him off for a second booking at the hour mark. For the West Ham loanee, it was best to leave that for the professionals. “I wanted to play the ball with the toe, I don't know if that was a yellow. I have no idea about that,” Füllkrug said about his challenge on Philipp Sander inside Gladbach's penalty box. “The referee has to decide that. A lot of little things were called against us. We take it as it comes. And now it turned out that I was allowed to play the whole game – great!" Werder Bremen's managing director Clemens Fritz also echoed Thioune and Füllkrug's dissatisfaction with the performance. “We didn’t play well today. We struggled to get into the game, were too passive and made a lot of mistakes. We were nowhere near our best today, but we still managed to fight back. All things considered, we have to be satisfied with a point because our performance wasn’t good enough to beat Gladbach.” the former defender said after the game.

top.title: Airlines losing passengers to travel stress, SITA warns
top.description: By Dickson Omobola Global air transport technology company, SITA, has said travel-related stress is discouraging people from travelling, leading to lost bookings and revenue for airlines. SITA’s 2026 Passenger IT Insights said a survey of nearly 8,000 travellers across 24 countries, four in 10 (42 per cent) have decided against taking a trip because they expected the experience to be too stressful. However, SITA’s Chief Executive Officer, David Lavorel, said the air transport industry could recover bookings and revenue lost to travel-related stress by deploying technology to give passengers greater visibility and control at every stage of their journeys. The survey also found that passengers increasingly expect technology to provide solutions, with eight in 10 believing it can reduce the stress associated with air travel. For airlines, the lost bookings are particularly significant because they involve some of their most valuable customers. Six in 10 frequent flyers have abandoned plans to travel because of anticipated stress. More than half of travellers under 30, the next generation of frequent flyers, have also done so. These two groups are also the most confident that technology can make air travel less stressful, with 89 per cent of frequent flyers and 86 per cent of travellers under 30 expressing confidence in its potential. Lavorel said: “Every trip we win back is a seat filled, a parking space sold and a coffee bought. Travellers are telling us where the stress comes from: delays, queues and worrying about their bags. Most of it comes down to not knowing what happens next. When airlines, airports, ground handlers and border agencies share what they know, passengers can see what is coming before they have to ask.” The post Airlines losing passengers to travel stress, SITA warns appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: ‘My stance is...’: Patrick Queen shares what his relationship with Aaron Rodgers is like now
top.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images The Aaron Rodgers situation has made this a very difficult week for the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback fell out with coach Mike McCarthy, then went on the Pat McAfee Show and had a go at him before being released by the organisation. Rodgers was a very popular teammate inside the locker room, so there have been theories on how the players would react to his behaviour following his exit. For Patrick Queen, however, there is no difference. Patrick Queen says his stance on Aaron Rodgers has not changed When there is a big split like in the case of Rodgers and McCarthy in the locker room, people would usually take sides. However, it looks like the Steelers have handled things brilliantly. On Friday, Pittsburgh produced one of their best performances of the season to beat the Denver Broncos 27-5. They were absolutely amazing. However, while speaking to the media after the game, several players showed their support for both parties. Queen is one such player, and he has spoken about his relationship with Rodgers now. He told Jenna Harner: “My stance is not going to change against Aaron. I love Aaron to death. Probably one of the coolest teammates I’ve ever had, just from the few conversations that we had. “My stance is not going to change on that. I don’t think anybody’s stance has changed on that.” That is the perfect way to handle the situation. Nobody should hate Rodgers because of the way he left, and at the same time, nobody should turn their back on coach McCarthy either. The Steelers showed on the field against the Broncos that they are fully behind their coach, and their relationship with Rodgers remains unaffected as well. The saga is well and truly over now, and it’s time for everyone to move on. The Vancouver Canucks are not doing well on the ice in 2026-27. However, this was an expected outcome. The Canucks have committed to a full rebuild, which has led to trade rumors around the likes of Elias Pettersson . Rebuilds can be a pain, of course. Ask the Detroit Red Wings how things are going right now. Vancouver is currently dead last in the NHL at this time. They are the only team in the league with fewer than 15 points as of November 28th. They have lost three games in a row and seven of their last 10. It’s not a fun time to be a Canucks fan. A lot of speculation this season will center on the core veterans. Pettersson has seemingly found his stride again, producing 23 points in his first 24 games this season. He is going to dominate Canucks trade rumors throughout the entirety of the season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He won’t be the only one mentioned, though. Brock Boeser leads the team in points . Jake DeBrusk has a solid track record of offensive success. Paul Cotter could be a decent depth piece as well. There are a lot of possibilities on the trade market for Vancouver this season. And they don’t need to rush things, either. A lot of their prime trade candidates are locked up long term. They can play the waiting game a bit before making their move. In saying this, there is one player who should be considered for a trade this season. He is one of the team’s stars, but he is also a valuable asset. It would be wise for Vancouver to at least gauge his market this year. Canucks’ Filip Hronek would attract trade interest Simon Fearn-Imagn Images In 2023, the Canucks took a big swing . They traded a first-round pick and a second-round pick to the Red Wings for Filip Hronek. It was a huge move at the time. Hronek showed promise as an offensive defenseman. He was also in his mid-20s and was about to play next to Quinn Hughes. Suffice it to say, things didn’t work out in the long term, at least as far as the team’s success is concerned. Hughes was traded by the Canucks last winter, and Vancouver entered its rebuild after one playoff run. Hronek has held up his end of the bargain, though. In 255 games with Vancouver, he has scored 19 goals and 148 points. He is producing at a higher points-per-game rate than he did in Detroit, and in 50 fewer games. His offensive ability is the same, if not better, than it was when he was with the Red Wings. Why would Vancouver trade him then? It’s simple. Hronek is about to enter his 30s, and he is on a long-term contract. The Canucks are unlikely to contend anytime soon. It would be well worth trading him for future assets that aid the rebuild. Hronek is a clear top-four defenseman who can spark his team from the blueline. There are a number of contenders who would love to have someone like him on the back end.

top.title: US, Italy disruptions expose urgency of Nigeria’s air navigation upgrade
top.description: By Dickson Omobola Following recent air traffic disruptions in the United States and Italy, linked to ageing infrastructure and telecommunications failures, calls have grown for Nigeria to urgently upgrade its air navigation infrastructure and equipment to avert similar incidents Many have warned that similar disruptions in the country could cause enormous financial losses, particularly for airlines already grappling with high operating costs, foreign exchange pressures, surging jet fuel prices and heavy taxation, while leaving passengers stranded and disrupt crucial travel plans. Beyond the immediate impact on flight schedules, they said airlines could incur additional costs from refunding affected passengers and providing care and assistance to those stranded. The concerns came after the unexpected incident in the United States on Friday, November 13, 2026, when the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA, imposed a nationwide ground stop that lasted several hours due to a telecommunications and equipment outage. United States Transportation Secretary, Sean Duffy, who attributed the problem to ageing infrastructure and instability in the country’s air traffic control radar and communications systems, said the wider economic impact of the disruption could run into billions of dollars. The communications failure affected all 22 air route traffic control centres, which guide aircraft across the country, leaving more than 10,000 flights delayed and at least 4,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware. The four largest US airlines, including American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and Southwest Airlines, could also suffer a combined $345m hit to their pre-tax earnings, according to brokerage firm Bernstein. Italy also experienced a major disruption in October, although the cause was different. An overnight fault in the geographic data transmission network supporting the country’s air traffic control system disrupted flight operations across several airports. The resulting delays and cancellations affected airports nationwide, including Rome Fiumicino, Milan, Bergamo, Naples, Venice, Palermo, Cagliari and Trieste. While intercontinental departures were prioritised, shorter-distance flights faced more interruptions. Urgent Against this backdrop, many aviation professionals across the country have said the need to accelerate the upgrade of the country’s air navigation infrastructure before similar failures occur cannot be over emphasised. Some of the equipment requiring attention include the Total Radar Coverage of Nigeria, TRACON, communication networks and navigation beacons. While the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency, NAMA, has identified some of the equipment as obsolete, lacking spare parts and operating beyond its expected lifespan, others have been described as overstretched. top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-SPORTING-MAN UTD - AFP Mauricio Pochettino has dismissed suggestions that he has become "too nice" since taking over at Manchester United, insisting he still possesses the aggressive edge that defined his time at Tottenham. The Argentine manager warned his squad that he is prepared to be strong and demanding as he attempts to overhaul the culture at Carrington. Redknapp questions Pochettino's edge at Old Trafford Former England midfielder Jamie Redknapp sparked the debate on The Overlap with Tim Sherwood, claiming the 54-year-old had lost the edge he showed at Southampton and Tottenham. Unprompted during Friday's press conference, Pochettino mounted a firm defence of his methods. He arrived a week ago with United stranded in the Premier League relegation zone after a dismal start. Pochettino draws line between 'nice' and good Redknapp contrasted Pochettino's past intensity with his relaxed demeanour at United. "When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked to me like he had that Argentinian dog in him," Redknapp said. "I look at him now and he's high fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice, I do." Pochettino rejected that view, insisting observers had misread his approach. "Do not misunderstand my words," Pochettino said. "Sometimes we are confusing two words that mean maybe something similar; nice and good. "I am not nice. I am not nice. We have to be good. That is a different thing," he insisted. "I am not nice. I am trying to be good. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. These two things are different." Longer sessions and 14-hour days to fix United's slump Pochettino has already lengthened training sessions beyond Michael Carrick's routine, though he knows rebuilding confidence amid fierce scrutiny is vital. "I think it's easy for us because we arrived one week ago," Pochettino said. "It's easy to arrive here with full energy and be positive and try to build that belief that we need. But of course for the players it's so tough because we cannot go away from all that noise that is around this football club. It's not only in this football club. It's in every single club that is not performing well. That is why it's so tough for the players." His relentless workload has even delayed a meeting with managerial role model Sir Alex Ferguson. "I didn't have the opportunity," Pochettino added. "I send all my admiration and love to him and I promise I will send a text. Look, it's not to say nothing. It's 12, 13, 14 hours spent here in the training ground and I didn't have time. You know, we are so fully focused on trying to provide everything, to start to improve our performances." top.title: WWE Star Bronson Reed Dies at 38 Weeks After He Was Thrown Off a Stage Through Tables
top.description: Bronson Reed/Insatgram WWE star Bronson Reed , whose real name was Jermaine Haley , has died. He was 38. WWE announced that he died on Friday, November 27, due to “medical complications,” but did not provide further details. “Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague,” the company said in a statement. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as all his friends, co-workers and fans.” His sudden death comes just three weeks after he was badly hurt in the ring. During WWE’s Crown Jewel event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on November 7, Reed was part of an angle during the World Tag Team Championship match in which Oba Femi slammed him off the stage and through a stack of tables, Uncrowned reported. Reed reportedly suffered multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney. He remained in a hospital in Saudi Arabia for more than a week, then underwent surgery and returned home to continue his recovery. The Crown Jewel event turned out to be his final WWE appearance. WWE has not said whether his injuries were connected to his death. Born in 1988 in Adelaide, South Australia, Reed grew up playing rugby and basketball but was drawn to professional wrestling from a young age. He made his in-ring debut in 2007 and spent years competing on the independent circuit in Australia and abroad, often under the name Jonah Rock. He first signed with WWE in 2019, reporting to its developmental brand, NXT, where he won the NXT North American Championship. After being released in 2021 amid budget cuts, he returned to the company and made his main roster debut in 2022. Reed went on to win the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in 2024 and most recently was part of the stable The Vision. top.title: Despite overall struggles, Texas QB Arch Manning leads one long drive against Texas A&M
top.description: Texas quarterback Arch Manning (16) walks the field after the Lone Star Showdown game against Texas A&M at Kyle Field on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026 in College Station, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) COLLEGE STATION - Earlier this week, Texas quarterback Arch Manning downplayed his role in the Longhorns' 17-7 win at College Station during the 2024 season . "I only played in like three plays that game," Manning told reporters. What Manning omitted was that one of those plays was a 15-yard touchdown run so it wasn't like his introduction to this rivalry was a nothingburger. But the point remains, Manning didn't play much during the Longhorns' last trip to College Station. That wasn't the case Friday. MORE: Craig Way, after 25 years as radio voice of Texas football, still 'as good as it gets' GOLDEN: The SEC must cut its ties with rules-skirting LSU and move on Manning threw for 143 yards and a touchdown as Texas recorded a 16-6 victory at Kyle Field . Sixteen of Manning's 34 passes fell incomplete and he had a deflected pass get intercepted near the end zone in the fourth quarter. The Texas offense, which posted season-low totals in yards and points, produced points on four of its 11 drives. But three of those scores were Gianni Spetic field goals. Texas A&M , however, was held to 234 yards by the UT defense. "That pick, I can't do that in that situation. I've got to run and try and get in the end zone. If not, kick the field goal," said Manning, who also led UT to a 27-17 win over Texas A&M in Austin last year. "But defense had our back all night, and they're going to continue to do that going forward." Manning did direct Texas on a 12-play drive that ended with Cam Coleman 's 3-yard touchdown catch. During an 88-yard drive that accounted for 36.4% of its offense for the evening, Manning completed all six of his attempts and also converted a 3rd-and-3 attempt with a 4-yard run. "I think we had just a really good rhythm in that drive," Texas center Connor Robertson said. View this post on Instagram A post shared by hookem.com (@hookemdotcom) Manning, Texas to meet Georgia in the SEC Championship Game For the season, Manning has thrown for 2,628 yards, 22 touchdowns and 11 interceptions while completing 64.9% of his passes. Manning will next attempt to join Paul Campbell (1949), Walter Fondren (1957), Bobby Lackey (1958) and Sam Ehlinger (2018) as the Texas quarterbacks that have led the Longhorns to a win over Georgia. Texas lost to the Bulldogs twice during the 2024 season with Quinn Ewers as its starter, and Manning was leading Texas during last season's 35-10 loss in Athens . "(Winning a conference title was) one of our goals before the season, and we're going to make the most out of it," Manning said. "Excited to go to Atlanta and play Georgia. They're kind of the standard. They've been in the SEC championship a lot of times. So we're excited for the challenge." Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman.

top.title: How Liverpool finally unlocked Alexander Isak to solve big problem
top.description: As Liverpool prepare to make their shortest journey of the season, Alexander Isak has come a long way in a few months. The fact he is leaving Anfield, even if it is only about two-and-a-half miles to Hill Dickinson Stadium, for Sunday’s Merseyside derby against Everton may bode well for an increasingly impressive traveller – the misfit who has become a mainstay. Since his unhappy return to Newcastle in the season opener, when Isak was barracked by the supporters who used to adore him, the Swedish striker has played in six away games and scored in each; indeed, of his 10 goals under Andoni Iraola , only two have come at Anfield. There may be some significance in the identity of the last Liverpool player to score in six straight away matches: Mohamed Salah , and if Isak is not a direct replacement for a right winger in one respect, he has been charged with taking on the Egyptian’s mantle as Liverpool’s scorer in chief. Alexander Isak has been tasked with replacing Mohamed Salah at Liverpool (PA) Even in Isak’s decidedly difficult debut year at Anfield , Liverpool may note two-thirds of his meagre tally of three league goals came away. Since Iraola took the reins, however, Isak has become his king of the road. The head coach admitted he is unsure why. “I don’t have any clear reason, honestly,” he said. “I think the way we play is the same whether away or at home. We know we have to go for the games either way. So I think it is just a coincidence. I don’t think there is a big difference in performance away or at home.” There may, however, be a difference in the context, when opponents open up and allow a side with Liverpool’s counter-attacking pace – wingers as speedy as Bradley Barcola , Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha , and a striker as quick as Isak – to break. nigeria.title: 2027: APC, APGA stakeholders unite for Tinubu’s re-election in Anambra
nigeria.description: Stakeholders of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) in Orumba South Local Government Area of Anambra State have agreed to work together to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. The stakeholders also pledged to support Governor Chukwuma Charles Soludo’s position backing Tinubu’s second-term ambition. The resolution was reached at a joint stakeholders’ meeting held on Saturday, November 28, 2026, and convened by the Chairman of Orumba South Local Government, Hon. Shedrack Azubuike, in collaboration with Booth 2 Booth with Bola Tinubu, an APC support group led by its National Coordinator, Mr Ikechukwu Madu. At the meeting, the stakeholders agreed to strengthen political cooperation, unity and mutual understanding between the two parties, stressing the importance of working across party lines in pursuit of shared political and developmental interests. A major outcome of the meeting was the decision to support Soludo’s position on Tinubu’s re-election and mobilise grassroots support across Orumba South. To achieve this, the stakeholders resolved to establish a joint APC–APGA mobilisation committee to coordinate political engagement and grassroots mobilisation across the 18 wards of the local government area. They also agreed to promote peaceful political coexistence, political tolerance and constructive engagement, while sustaining regular consultations and collaborative initiatives for the development of Orumba South. The stakeholders commended Azubuike and Madu for initiating the engagement, describing the meeting as an opportunity to strengthen cooperation among political stakeholders and establish a common platform around shared objectives. Those present included the Deputy National Coordinator of Booth 2 Booth, Mr Jafar Abdulahi Ibrahim; the group’s Anambra State Coordinator, Mr Paschal Candle; and the APC Anambra State Organising Secretary, Mr Izuchukwu Okeke. The meeting ended with a reaffirmation of the stakeholders’ commitment to sustained APC–APGA cooperation, support for Soludo’s position on Tinubu’s re-election and grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. nigeria.title: Airlines losing passengers to travel stress, SITA warns
nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Global air transport technology company, SITA, has said travel-related stress is discouraging people from travelling, leading to lost bookings and revenue for airlines. SITA’s 2026 Passenger IT Insights said a survey of nearly 8,000 travellers across 24 countries, four in 10 (42 per cent) have decided against taking a trip because they expected the experience to be too stressful. However, SITA’s Chief Executive Officer, David Lavorel, said the air transport industry could recover bookings and revenue lost to travel-related stress by deploying technology to give passengers greater visibility and control at every stage of their journeys. The survey also found that passengers increasingly expect technology to provide solutions, with eight in 10 believing it can reduce the stress associated with air travel. For airlines, the lost bookings are particularly significant because they involve some of their most valuable customers. Six in 10 frequent flyers have abandoned plans to travel because of anticipated stress. More than half of travellers under 30, the next generation of frequent flyers, have also done so. These two groups are also the most confident that technology can make air travel less stressful, with 89 per cent of frequent flyers and 86 per cent of travellers under 30 expressing confidence in its potential. Lavorel said: “Every trip we win back is a seat filled, a parking space sold and a coffee bought. Travellers are telling us where the stress comes from: delays, queues and worrying about their bags. Most of it comes down to not knowing what happens next. When airlines, airports, ground handlers and border agencies share what they know, passengers can see what is coming before they have to ask.” The post Airlines losing passengers to travel stress, SITA warns appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: US, Italy disruptions expose urgency of Nigeria’s air navigation upgrade
nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Following recent air traffic disruptions in the United States and Italy, linked to ageing infrastructure and telecommunications failures, calls have grown for Nigeria to urgently upgrade its air navigation infrastructure and equipment to avert similar incidents Many have warned that similar disruptions in the country could cause enormous financial losses, particularly for airlines already grappling with high operating costs, foreign exchange pressures, surging jet fuel prices and heavy taxation, while leaving passengers stranded and disrupt crucial travel plans. Beyond the immediate impact on flight schedules, they said airlines could incur additional costs from refunding affected passengers and providing care and assistance to those stranded. The concerns came after the unexpected incident in the United States on Friday, November 13, 2026, when the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA, imposed a nationwide ground stop that lasted several hours due to a telecommunications and equipment outage. United States Transportation Secretary, Sean Duffy, who attributed the problem to ageing infrastructure and instability in the country’s air traffic control radar and communications systems, said the wider economic impact of the disruption could run into billions of dollars. The communications failure affected all 22 air route traffic control centres, which guide aircraft across the country, leaving more than 10,000 flights delayed and at least 4,000 cancelled, according to FlightAware. The four largest US airlines, including American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and Southwest Airlines, could also suffer a combined $345m hit to their pre-tax earnings, according to brokerage firm Bernstein. Italy also experienced a major disruption in October, although the cause was different. An overnight fault in the geographic data transmission network supporting the country’s air traffic control system disrupted flight operations across several airports. The resulting delays and cancellations affected airports nationwide, including Rome Fiumicino, Milan, Bergamo, Naples, Venice, Palermo, Cagliari and Trieste. While intercontinental departures were prioritised, shorter-distance flights faced more interruptions. nigeria.title: Evil or Helping Angel? How one librarian keeps AI honest and accurate
nigeria.description: By Ebele Orakpo The widespread adoption of Artificial Intelligence has sparked growing concerns over its societal impact. Critics warn that heavy reliance on AI weakens critical thinking, creativity, and human mentorship in education while widening the digital divide. Also, creative industries face job displacement, copyright theft, and unauthorised likeness cloning. Digital markets are flooded with mass-produced AI content, devaluing human artistry. In this chat with Vanguard, Mr. Amed Demirhan, one of the pioneers of e-library worldwide and the General Manager/Director of the Barzani National Memorial Library and Museum in Kurdistan, Iraq, deviates from the norm of merely learning how to operate AI and advocates for training AI to maximize its output. The former Director of Library Services, American University of Nigeria, Yola, argues that this proactive approach can preserve jobs previously considered vulnerable to automation and concludes that human intelligence is still the ultimate. Excerpts: Training the AI Like many new innovations, AI sharply divides public opinion. While some praise it as an exceptional breakthrough, others view it as very dangerous, raising serious ethical concerns like information manipulation. However, I believe AI remains one of the most effective research assistants one can get. AI capabilities AI can perform complex tasks associated with human intelligence, including learning, adapting, analyzing information, problem- solving, and remembering. Within seconds, it can browse billions of global, multilingual records and resources—far exceeding the collections of the largest physical national libraries—to retrieve requested information. However, as a human creation, AI reflects all human imperfections. Just like any student, researcher, or research assistant, it requires proper training to become truly effective. Otherwise, when you ask a question or direct it to gather research information, it will retrieve overwhelming, unhelpful results, much like sailing across the vast ocean without a compass or clear direction. Set the rules Training AI with information literacy standards, including evaluating source content, verifying facts, checking author and publisher credibility, and citing properly, makes it far more effective for academic researchers. Beyond these foundational standards, we can add tailored, research-specific rules to target unique project needs. The AI operates strictly within a structured framework rather than searching randomly if instructed to retain these guidelines. My rules I rely on a strict set of principles when working with AI; I call these “my rules” because, much like students, AI does not always follow instructions automatically. Instead of constantly repeating my guidelines when requesting research, I simply tell it to follow “my rules.” Usually, it remembers the standards and corrects its output. nigeria.title: 3-year-old girl defiled at school, expelled; mother cries for justice
nigeria.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure For Mrs Usman, the day started like any other school day. Her husband went to pick up their two children from Oakland Kids Nursery and Primary School, Oda Road, Akure, not knowing that their little daughter would come home with a story that would change their family forever. It was at home that evening that the truth began to unfold. Their 3-year-old daughter, a KG II pupil, quietly told her elder brother, who is in Nursery II, that a boy in her class had touched her. How father heard Her father overheard the conversation. Worried, he called the little girl and asked her to explain. She mentioned the name of her classmate and said he touched her private part. Her father immediately called her mother. At first, Mrs. Usman thought it might be a child’s misunderstanding. But when she got home after 7pm, she checked her daughter’s pants and saw blood stains. And when the child urinated, she cried out in pain. Asked again who touched her, she repeated the same name. Asked why she did not tell her teachers, the little girl said she was afraid she would be beaten. Nightmare, search for healthcare That night, the family rushed to a nearby pharmacy. The pharmacists said they could not handle such a case and advised them to see a paediatrician. The next day, October 28, Mrs. Usman took her daughter to the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Akure. After examination, doctors confirmed the child had been defiled. With the medical report in hand, she went straight to the school to report. ‘CCTV not working’ According to her, the proprietor expressed shock. But when she asked to see the CCTV footage of the classroom, she was told the camera was not working. She also asked that the parents of the boy be informed. She said the school did not do so until the following day, after she raised her voice. The boy’s mother, on hearing the news, was said to have queried the school for not informing her earlier. Mother’s cry Mrs. Usman said she only asked for one thing: that her daughter should not remain in the same class as the boy. Instead, she said the proprietor suggested moving her daughter to Nursery I, where she would repeat the class if she could not cope. “Why should my daughter, the victim, be the one to be moved?” she asked. The situation worsened when the boy’s father allegedly called her, accusing her of making a false allegation and threatening her, saying, don’t bite more than what you can chew.” Mrs. Usman said the proprietor later admitted the school gave the man her phone number so they could talk as parents. Police Feeling threatened, she went to the police station. She was directed to the Gender Based Violence agency in the state. She later petitioned the State Commissioner of Police. nigeria.title: Messi’s defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs
nigeria.description: Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday. Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida. The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup. For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested. Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio. German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar. The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair. Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012. nigeria.description: By Benjamin Njoku When Vanguard encountered Pete Edochie, the Lion of Africa in his den on two different occasions, it was never just an interview.It was an audience with a king. Ebubedike sat on his throne, spoke in proverbs, laughed loudly, sipped from a glass of fresh palm wine and dropped revelations that have now become timeless. Those conversations carried the full weight of Pete Edochie and what he represented on the big screen and in real life. The first encounter was in a hotel room in Owerri, in 2015, where he displayed rare qualities that set him apart from his contemporaries: his sense of humour, his values as a father and an actor, as well as his impeccable command of the English language. The second encounter was at his Trans Ekulu, Enugu residence in 2022. During the encounter, Ebubedike was in his element. His imposing duplex dotted with images of his artistic journey, laurels and his image as the godfather of the Nigerian movie industry set the tone for the timeless conversation. In real life, he was a man of honour and class. When you were with him, you would not be tired of laughing. Intermittently, he would smile to encourage his guests while sharing his story passionately with them. As we recount those encounters spanning our august visit to him in Enugu in 2022, his repeated battles with rumours of his death, his reflections on Nollywood, family and mortality, now read like a final testament after his death on Wednesday, due to prolonged battle with prostate cancer. nigeria.title: Uduere Killings in Delta: Six trucks of policemen, yet bullets still found targets
nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi The sound of gunfire shattered the campaign atmosphere at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, November 23. People who had gathered for a political rally suddenly scrambled for safety. Women ran, campaigners scattered and, in the ensuing chaos, bullets found human targets. By the time the shooting stopped, families had lost loved ones, several people critically wounded and communities plunged into mourning. Among the disturbing details was that six truckloads of policemen had reportedly been deployed to provide security. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, put their number at close to 50. Yet, according to accounts from both political camps, the violence escalated despite the robust security presence. The tragedy has since generated competing accusations between the All Progressives Congress, APC, and the National Democratic Congress, NDC. Beneath the political blame game are grieving families, wounded survivors and ordinary citizens asking why a political gathering should become a death trap. A Trail Of Troubled Political Gatherings Uduere was not an isolated incident in the build-up to Delta 2027 elections. September 18, a one-million-man march organised by the NDC in the Warri-Effurun axis was disrupted by violence, leaving persons wounded. An AK-47 allegedly recovered from a suspect identified as Collins became a subject of controversy between the party and police. The NDC alleged the suspect was released the following day, a claim that formed part of its subsequent complaints about police handling of the incident. October 3, the party held a 10,000-man march against hunger in Ughelli. The following day, the Ughelli North Local Government Council, chaired by Chief Jaro Egbo, issued a notice, sealed the business premises and impounded truck belonging to Tobore Alex Agbah, who led the march. Agbah would later become one of the victims of the Uduere violence. November 7, another NDC one-million-man march in Asaba ended in violence, with one fatality recorded. The recurrence of disturbances has fuelled allegations that NDC gatherings are being targeted by political opponents allegedly linked to the ruling APC. Delta State Commissioner for Information, Charles Aniagwu, however, rejected the suggestion of a pattern. “It’s not a pattern, because when you talk about a pattern, it means that it’s continuously and then you are linking it to be able to join one to the other,” he said. He argued: “The NDC is not being attacked, there are a number of local governments where we have not had any disturbances. The APC in Delta is holding sway, the underdogs in this case are the members of the NDC who are few.” But NDC governorship candidate, Chris Iyovwaye, disagreed, recalling the September incident. “Another thug of APC was caught with an AK-47 and was handed over to the police. nigeria.description: By Juliet Umeh As the 2027 general elections draw closer, political defections, shifting alliances and questions about leadership are beginning to shape the debate over who should govern Nigeria for another four years. But for former Lagos State Governor, Mr Babatunde Fashola, one important test for anyone seeking to lead the country is the ability to build relationships, work with others and remain committed to a political team, even in difficult times. Fashola believes President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated these qualities, arguing that his ability to retain political associates and bring former opponents into his camp makes him better placed to manage Nigeria’s diversity. In a pointed challenge to opposition leaders, the former governor asked voters to examine what happened to the people who worked with other presidential contenders and why many of them were no longer in their political camps. Speaking during an interview on Arise Television, Fashola said political relationships should serve as a reference point for assessing the leadership capacity of those seeking the presidency. “Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question. For those who want to vote, where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him when he was governor still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so, out of office, when he wasn’t a president,” he said. According to him, the ability to work with people is essential for anyone entrusted with managing a country as diverse as Nigeria. “If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team. And you don’t just get up and jump away when there’s a crisis in the fold,” he said. Fashola noted that Tinubu remained in the All Progressives Congress, APC, despite internal disagreements, while some political leaders had abandoned parties that helped build their political careers. He also pointed to Tinubu’s ability to bring former opponents into his political fold, describing it as evidence of his capacity to build relationships across political divides. “Not just those who worked with him before, those who opposed him are now working with him. That’s how he has built a coalition of 30 state governors from one state, from Lagos. And that is profound, whether you like him or not,” he said. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, will today run a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), about seven weeks before the 2027 general election. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser, ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. He said the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV, v,lidation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. Amupitan said the Commission had procured new accreditation machines and set a lower voter threshold for the actual election in January. “INEC will deploy over 1.41 million ad hoc personnel alongside 57,000 newly procured Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices, calibrated at a reduced threshold of 850 voters per machine,” he said. He told the gathering that the rehearsal was as much a test of coordination with security agencies as of technology. “Strategy without rehearsal is merely aspiration,” he said. The INEC chairman called on the Commission’s Resident Electoral Commissioners and the Commissioners of Police in the states to take part fully. “I urge all Resident Electoral Commissioners and Commissioners of Police to treat November 28 as a full-scale operational rehearsal: test your communication lines, evaluate rapid-response times around mock polling centres, and identify any logistical or security blind spots while there is still ample time to resolve them,” he said. INEC had earlier published the list of polling units selected for the nationwide mock accreditation exercise, naming 17,656 locations across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. The commission said the exercise is a “Mock Accreditation and Result Upload Exercise” using the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS. Abaji, Bwari, Gwagwalada, Kuje and Kwali have 20 each, while the Municipal Area Council has 24. nigeria.title: Death on the River: Some who came for rescue were more interested in stealing phones, bags, money — Survivor
nigeria.description: By Emem Idio, Yenagoa Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled for survival as the overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie Community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun who is married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat that was unfit to carry the large number of passengers. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but when none was available, a local boat was brought to convey them. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after boarding, raising fears among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from one side to another, forcing passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, creating panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. She said when she resurfaced, she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, apparently to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young lady die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she was particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said, “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. People were shouting, and before we knew what was happening, the boat collapsed and started sinking.” Narrating how she managed to save herself and her children, Silas said she used her swimming skills to guide her son through the water. nigeria.description: *Torn between Tinubu’s reforms, Obi’s change message, Atiku’s comeback *Say, Tinubu has capacity to take bold decisions, Obi possesses good credentials, Atiku may reduce petrol price By Dayo Johnson, Regional Editor, South West The 2027 general election is barely two months away. Some of the political parties that will be on the ballot have already hit the streets campaigning. Many of the candidates are seeking to renew the mandate that was given to them in 2023. Others who didn’t make it in the last election are back again hoping to succeed this time around. The candidates are making fresh promises. The electorate, on their part, have been speaking on what will inform their choice of who to vote for during the elections and their responses reveal an electorate pulled in sharply different directions. We did not embark on data collation but randomly spoke with some Nigerians in the southwest, southeast, south south and the northern region of the country. Backers of President Bola Tinubu defend him on his capacity to push restructuring and take bold decisions, arguing that but for him the economy would have collapsed completely, even as some concede that his reforms have yet to ease hardship. But they have hope and argue that Nigeria would be better under Tinubu in the years to come. A few voices break from the Obi-Tinubu argument entirely, backing Atiku, the ADC, or local candidates on performance. In markets, campuses and government offices, a strong current of support for Peter Obi runs through everyday voters- market women, traders, students and civil servants, who point to the rising cost of living, government borrowing and hunger for change. Another powerful theme in their responses is the widespread distrust of the electoral system itself. Many voters express lack of faith in the process and expect politicians to rig and litigate rather than accept the people’s verdict, even as the spate of ongoing violence is already scaring them. Professionals frame their choices more cautiously arguing that they will be guided by candidates’ positions on sustainable development, Niger Delta equity and resource justice rather than ethnicity or party. From conviction to civic duty to indecision, the message from the streets is clear: a wary electorate is watching, and waiting to decide amidst fears of violence. But some did with high expectations, considering his antecedents both in private and public sectors. Three years and seven months down the line, Governor Peter Ndubuisi Mbah’s scorecard speaks for itself. No long ago, the administration unveiled 10,000 milestone achievements of the government. A critical analysis of his achievements reveals that significant progress has been recorded across all critical sectors. Since he mounted the saddle of leadership, Gov. Anchored on his administration’s eight-year development vision, Mbah seeks to grow the state’s economy from approximately $4.4 billion to at least $30 billion in four to eight years, while tackling poverty through investments in critical sectors. At the heart of this vision is the recognition that sustainable economic growth cannot be achieved without adequate infrastructure, a productive agricultural sector, accessible healthcare and quality education, among others. These sectors form critical pillars of the administration’s development strategy, with interventions designed not only to address existing deficits, but also to prepare the state for emerging economic opportunities. Mbah has, at various fora, made it known to whoever cared to listen, that his administration was determined to move beyond policy pronouncements to measurable outcomes that could actually improve the living conditions of residents. Meanwhile , in x-raying Mbah’s scorecard, our analytical lens will today focus on four critical sectors: infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare and education. Education: 268 Smart Green Schools to transform learning Governor has left no one in doubt about his passion for education as veritable for transforming the society and building its economy. He has often held that no nation can develop beyond its human capital. But has proved that it was mere rhetoric. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry.
