entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Did you grow up watching Pete Edochie in Nollywood films? Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Directed by David Orere , the acclaimed television miniseries marked Edochie’s first professional acting role and saw him bring the proud, fierce, and deeply conflicted Umuofia warrior to life with remarkable nuance. His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. It was a response that reflected the thinking behind HÉYCH, a brand seeking to occupy an important space in the market by making well-made, stylish clothing accessible without asking consumers to compromise on quality. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. For Ebigbeyi, local production is as much about business efficiency as it is about building something sustainable within Nigeria. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Former Barcelona forward urges patience with Real Madrid’s South American stars
sports.description: Former Barcelona forward urges patience with Real Madrid’s South American stars Vitor Roque has been enjoying life ever since his return to Brazil. Since joining Palmeiras in 2025, the forward has racked up 29 goals, and his market value has also gone up. This comes on the back of a disastrous spell at Barcelona, where the player struggled to prove himself and eventually left the club permanently in 2025. In light of his success, the former Barcelona forward was recently asked about the lack of patience from European clubs when it comes to talents from South America. Vitor Roque on Endrick and Mastantuono Roque believes players like Endrick need more time. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) When asked about the South American talents, the interviewer particularly referenced two Real Madrid players: Endrick and Franco Mastantuono. Both players had joined Real Madrid in the recent past. While Mastantuono had to settle for a loan at Fiorentina, Endrick is also struggling with a lack of game time despite being a part of Jose Mourinho’s setup this season. Keeping that in mind, Roque urged more patience with these players. “People believe that young people arrive and we have to start playing 100%, giving everything, doing our best football, but it is not. It takes patience. Sometimes we don’t have the adaptation time we need,” he said (h/t Diario AS ). The former Barcelona forward pointed out how language and culture can also be a problem for young South American stars. “We are very young and speaking a new language is very difficult. Sometimes it is important to have the support of the coach and I when I went to Barcelona I did not have it. They barely talked to me, you know? “So I think you have to keep that in mind and a lot of people don’t see it that way, they think you have to be prepared from the first minute ,” he added. What’s next for Endrick and Mastantuono? Mastantuono’s fate will be decided at the end of the season. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Fortunately, it appears Real Madrid are ready to bide their time with both Endrick and Mastantuono. Especially in the case of Endrick, the club have not shown any indication of permanently parting ways with the forward. They are, in fact, ready to block a January exit for the Brazilian international, who is rated highly by coach Mourinho. As for Mastantuono, the Argentine has shown glimpses of his talents at Fiorentina. But unless he breaks out in a big way like Nico Paz, it is unlikely Real Madrid will want to make him a part of the first-team setup next season.

sports.title: Atlético beat Viking 2-0 as both strikers score, but Sørloth injury hits Barcelona trip
sports.description: Atlético beat Viking 2-0 as both strikers score, but Sørloth injury hits Barcelona trip Alexander Sørloth and Julián Álvarez both ended goal droughts as Atlético Madrid beat Viking FK 2-0 to reach seven points in the Champions League. Sørloth's muscle injury now adds to an injury list that already includes Lookman, just as Atlético face Barcelona and PSV. Atlético Madrid’s win over Viking FK revived their hopes of a direct top-eight finish. Three league-phase games remain, and one of them is away to PSV. Both of Simeone’s leading strikers found the net. Yet the night also added a new name to the injury list. Sørloth broke the deadlock by firing in a pass from Alejandro Grimaldo. Five minutes later, Álvarez’s free-kick crept in at the near post. It was his 27th goal in the Champions League. It was also his first Champions League goal at the Metropolitano in 210 days. The strike was his third of the 2026-27 season: one in LaLiga and two in Europe. Grimaldo was named Player of the Match. Viking defender Henrik Falchener was sent off late in the game. Win steadies a European campaign that stalled against Bayern The result follows an uneven league phase. Atlético opened with a 2-1 defeat at Liverpool. They then beat Manchester United 2-0 at home. A 1-1 draw at Stuttgart followed. Bayern München then won 0-2 at the Metropolitano on 3 November. That home defeat was unusual. Before kick-off against Viking, Atlético had won 11 of their previous 14 home matches in the group stage or league phase. They lost the other three. The victory over the Norwegian side returned them to winning ways in front of their own supporters. The mood inside the stadium was not entirely positive, however. Some home fans whistled Álvarez when he was substituted, even though he had scored. Sørloth injury leaves Simeone short before Barcelona and PSV Sørloth went off limping after 71 minutes. He had taken a heavy knock against the post and left the field with an overload, the club said on 26 November. No date has been set for his return. He will do physiotherapy and gym rehabilitation. The expected absence is significant. ESPN Deportes expects him to miss at least the games against Elche, Barcelona, Real Betis, Valencia and PSV. That would rule him out of the visit to Eindhoven. His injury adds to a list that already includes Lookman. The forward has a high-grade knee sprain. Simeone is therefore short of attacking options for a demanding run of fixtures. The first major test comes at the Spotify Camp Nou on Wednesday 2 December, with kick-off at 20:30 GMT (21:30 in Spain). Viking host Feyenoord on 8 December. Atlético’s next Champions League game follows a day later, away to PSV Eindhoven on 9 December. sports.title: ‘He just…’ – Luka Doncic addresses throwing wristband at Spurs fan before post-game altercation
sports.description: Photo by Ben Liebenberg/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers star Luka Doncic found himself in some post-game controversy after the team’s 99-96 loss to the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Cup. Doncic had a mixed night in which he stuffed the box score with 31 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three steals. However, he also took 31 shots, shot 1-13 from three-point range, and left with a high-profile loss to their rivals in San Antonio. As Doncic left the court, he appeared to throw his wristband at some Spurs fans courtside, who did not appreciate the gesture. As Doncic went to pick the wristband back up, a fan shoved him back, leading to a highly contentious postgame moment. Luka Doncic addresses what went down in post-game shove with Spurs fan Doncic spoke to the media after the game and explained what went down, revealing that this is something he does every game, and he got shoved by the fan when he heard them say they didn’t want it and went to retrieve it. “I just threw my wristband like I do almost every game, and then I heard she didn’t want it, so I went back to grab it, and he just pushed me, and then I gave it to somebody else.” Anyone who has seen Doncic play in Dallas or Los Angeles knows he does throw his wristbands at fans after the game, usually because they want to take it home with them as memorabilia. Mavericks fan and the lead producer for LeBron James’ ‘Mind the Game’ podcast, Jason Gallagher , revealed that Doncic has done the same towards his child, but in a way that was always considered Doncic being charitable with fans. “He nonchalantly throws wristbands/headbands at fans all the time. My kid has one! Tons of players do that. It sure looks like he didn’t like what this woman said, so he went back and got it from a fan who didn’t want it. Then the dork shoved him lol.” Doncic seemed to aggressively throw the wristband, which went low and hit the woman that the Spurs fan presumably came to the game with, leading to the fan’s aggressive response when Doncic approached them to get the wristband back. The heightened tensions of this early-season marquee clash between Doncic and Victor Wembanyama’s Spurs seemed to have fans on edge, especially as this was a couple in Spurs jerseys who probably did not want Doncic’s wristband anyway, and disagreed with him throwing it towards them. sports.title: Thioune concedes Bremen fortunate to draw Gladbach as West Ham loanee Füllkrug discusses potential red card incident
sports.description: Thioune concedes Bremen fortunate to draw Gladbach as West Ham loanee Füllkrug discusses potential red card incident With 13 points from their first five Weserstadion encounters, sixth-placed Werder Bremen were the overwhelming favorites against cellar-dwellers Borussia Mönchengladbach on Friday. However, it took two goals after the 85th-minute mark to maintain their unbeaten home record. “Today, we got some entertaining football," Daniel Thioune started his post-match interview with Sky Sports on a positive note. "In the end, you have to be happy if you equalize. Gladbach could have wrapped up the game earlier. “We even had a chance to make it 4-3 at the end, that's crazy. That would have been too much. If you get a point based on your mentality, I'm satisfied." Thioune added regarding Cedric Itten’s missed chance after Niclas Füllkrug's injury-time equalizer. The Germany international extended his lead at the top of the scoring chart with his 11th strike since coming back to Bremen on an initial loan deal. The 33-year-old has 14 goals in all competitions, including scoring in every game at Weserstadion. “I don't think Gladbach quite deserves their position in the table,” Füllkrug praised the opposing team after the match. “The last few games have always been close. They played well against Dortmund, and they played well again today, giving us some problems.” Despite the late turnaround, the ex-BVB man wasn't satisfied with their own performance. “When you play the way we have been, expectations rise for yourself. Of course, I'm disappointed. We were far too sloppy, and lost possession far too often. We left room for improvement there today. We have to be honest about that." Füllkrug was fortunate to repeat his Dortmund heroics because Felix Zwayer could've easily sent him off for a second booking at the hour mark. For the West Ham loanee, it was best to leave that for the professionals. “I wanted to play the ball with the toe, I don't know if that was a yellow. I have no idea about that,” Füllkrug said about his challenge on Philipp Sander inside Gladbach's penalty box. “The referee has to decide that. A lot of little things were called against us. We take it as it comes. And now it turned out that I was allowed to play the whole game – great!" Werder Bremen's managing director Clemens Fritz also echoed Thioune and Füllkrug's dissatisfaction with the performance. “We didn’t play well today. We struggled to get into the game, were too passive and made a lot of mistakes. We were nowhere near our best today, but we still managed to fight back. All things considered, we have to be satisfied with a point because our performance wasn’t good enough to beat Gladbach.” the former defender said after the game.

sports.title: WWE Star Bronson Reed Dies at 38 Weeks After He Was Thrown Off a Stage Through Tables
sports.description: Bronson Reed/Insatgram WWE star Bronson Reed , whose real name was Jermaine Haley , has died. He was 38. WWE announced that he died on Friday, November 27, due to “medical complications,” but did not provide further details. “Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague,” the company said in a statement. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as all his friends, co-workers and fans.” His sudden death comes just three weeks after he was badly hurt in the ring. During WWE’s Crown Jewel event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on November 7, Reed was part of an angle during the World Tag Team Championship match in which Oba Femi slammed him off the stage and through a stack of tables, Uncrowned reported. Reed reportedly suffered multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney. He remained in a hospital in Saudi Arabia for more than a week, then underwent surgery and returned home to continue his recovery. The Crown Jewel event turned out to be his final WWE appearance. WWE has not said whether his injuries were connected to his death. Born in 1988 in Adelaide, South Australia, Reed grew up playing rugby and basketball but was drawn to professional wrestling from a young age. He made his in-ring debut in 2007 and spent years competing on the independent circuit in Australia and abroad, often under the name Jonah Rock. He first signed with WWE in 2019, reporting to its developmental brand, NXT, where he won the NXT North American Championship. After being released in 2021 amid budget cuts, he returned to the company and made his main roster debut in 2022. Reed went on to win the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in 2024 and most recently was part of the stable The Vision. The fact he is leaving Anfield, even if it is only about two-and-a-half miles to Hill Dickinson Stadium, for Sunday’s Merseyside derby against Everton may bode well for an increasingly impressive traveller – the misfit who has become a mainstay. Since his unhappy return to Newcastle in the season opener, when Isak was barracked by the supporters who used to adore him, the Swedish striker has played in six away games and scored in each; indeed, of his 10 goals under Andoni Iraola , only two have come at Anfield. Since Iraola took the reins, however, Isak has become his king of the road. The head coach admitted he is unsure why. “I don’t have any clear reason, honestly,” he said. “I think the way we play is the same whether away or at home. Now, though, it's becoming increasingly difficult for anyone but Brazil to win. On Saturday evening at the historic Centenario stadium in Montevideo, Palmeiras will look to make it eight Libertadores triumphs in a row for Brasileiro Serie A sides - and 26 overall. There is a very strong Estudiantes side standing in their way, and the Argentines have already taken out Corinthians and defending champions Flamengo on their route to the final, meaning victory is by no means a given for Palmeiras. However, even if Estudiantes were to upset the odds in Uruguay, there's very little evidence to suggest that Brazil's overall dominance of Libertadores is going to end anytime soon... 'The potential is spectacular' The City Football Group (CFG) is one of several foreign groups to have invested in Brazilian clubs since a key structural rule change In a way, Brazil bossing the Libertadores is perfectly natural. The country has a population of roughly 214 million people - almost as many as the rest of South America combined (226m) - and it also boasts one of the 10 biggest economies in the world. When it came to the continental competition, though, Brazil consistently punched well below its weight. There was an impressive streak of six trophies in eight years in the 1990s, and four in a row between 2010 and 2013, but, for the most part, the country failed to turn its clear numerical and economic advantages into sustained success - until now. Brazilian clubs haven't just won the past seven Copa Libertadores; Palmeiras' participation in Saturday's game in Uruguay means that they also now account for 13 of the past 16 finalists. And why is this? Money, essentially, because Brazilian football is booming. Only Premier League clubs spent more money during the 2026 winter transfer window than their Brazilian counterparts - something that would have been unimaginable during the pandemic, when it became clear that many of the country's top-tier teams were heavily in debt. Instead, a capitulation at the hands of Spain in June condemned the European champions to the play-off route, where they are having to overcome lower-ranked opponents with familiar playing styles in must-win games that it can be hard to learn much from. One could forgive Wiegman for looking at the European teams that did secure qualification in June with envy. While her England side faced a Greece team ranked outside the world's top 50 last month, Spain took on the United States in a double-header , Germany clashed with Australia and Japan, and Denmark flew to Canada. All four of those nations sit in the top 15 in FIFA's rankings. But as the old saying goes, when life gives you lemons, make lemonade. Games against Greece and Ukraine - the latter of whom England have already played twice this year, soundly beating them on both occasions - might not be stern tests against potential World Cup contenders, but Wiegman has been doing all she can to ensure there is plenty to learn from these games. Indeed, how she has approached these qualifiers so far could well give the Lionesses an even greater chance of winning the World Cup next summer. Seeking unpredictability Wiegman's England have become a little predictable in recent times, but a switch of shape in the October window indicated that could be changing For a while now, England have been quite predictable. The Lionesses almost always line up in a 4-2-3-1 shape and it's not difficult to correctly predict who will make up the majority of that XI, especially at a major tournament when the best XI is called upon. Of course, it doesn't mean they are easy to thwart and beat because of that, as their back-to-back European Championship titles show . But as Wiegman eyes World Cup glory, a little more unpredictability could go a long way. sports.description: Hristo Stoichkov Bulgaria Barcelona GFX - GOAL The Bulgarian may have won the Ballon d'Or in 1994 but he was always as temperamental as he was talented Hristo Stoichkov has always been immensely proud of the fact that he shares a first name with his grandfather. But he's also long enjoyed the religious connection. During the 1994 World Cup, he mused, "With this name, there's always been one [Christ] above, and one below. The one below also performs miracles." Blasphemous? Perhaps. But also arguably accurate. Bulgaria were certainly a revelation in the United States that summer, and Stoichkov’s performances heavenly. The man was no saint during his playing days, of course, as he admitted himself. There was a rage inside him, one that drove him all the way to the pinnacle of his profession, but also resulted in him repeatedly stepping over the line. "I was raised in the middle of the street," he once told reporters in Spain. "You learn certain things there..." Discipline obviously wasn't one of them. Indeed, his career could have ended shortly after it had begun. Cruyff's Ballon d'Or promise The Dutchman clashed constantly with the Bulgarian but knew that he had the potential to become the best in the world Stoichkov was still only a teenager when he was involved in a mass brawl in the Bulgarian Cup final that saw him promptly hit with a lifetime ban. However, his suspension was reduced to a solitary month on appeal and the CSKA Sofia striker quickly set about making the most of his reprieve. In 1990, he won the Golden Shoe after netting 38 times in 30 league games, which made a number of Europe's elite sit up and take notice. Little did they know, though, that Stoichkov was already bound for Barcelona, who had moved quickly to wrap up a deal for the Bulgarian after he netted three goals across the two legs of a European Cup Winners' Cup semi-final loss to the Catalans the year before. The transfer had been carried out in such secrecy that not even Stoichkov's wife or parents knew about the pre-contract agreement he'd signed with the Blaugrana at the tail end of 1989. However, it initially looked like Barca had made a gross error of judgement in signing such a combustible character, given Stoichkov was sent off against Real Madrid in the Supercopa de Espana shortly after arriving at Camp Nou – and then, to make matters much, much worse, stamped on the foot of match referee Urizar Azpitarte before leaving the pitch. technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. technology.description: The UK government has rejected calls for a UK-wide public consultation on the environmental impacts of AI datacenters, despite a petition attracting more than 39,000 signatures. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. In its response, published on November 23, the government ruled out the requested UK-wide environmental consultation, saying individual projects' impacts should be addressed through the planning process. It pointed instead to a separate consultation on its draft datacenter planning policy, open until January 8, 2027. "Datacenters are vital to the UK's digital economy. They underpin the digital services that people rely on every day, including public services, healthcare and the way people work. They also provide the infrastructure needed to develop and use AI," the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (BIST) says. "Building more capacity in the UK will support economic growth and innovation, while strengthening national resilience and ensuring the UK is well placed to realize the opportunities presented by AI." But it adds that the government recognizes the environmental impacts of bit barns are real and must be understood and mitigated, and this is one of the reasons why it established the Data Centre Covenant tests. This Covenant, published last month, sets out tests all compute sheds "are encouraged to meet," while "strategic datacenters" are required to meet them to qualify for additional government assistance. The government has yet to define which datacenters qualify as "strategic," saying it will publish further details and eligibility criteria in due course. Qualifying projects could receive help securing power and accelerating planning. Briefly, the Covenant tests are that operators cover any energy costs they create, so that communities do not have to pick up the bill; that they invest in local communities; adhere to the highest environmental standards; create jobs and drive reindustrialization; and provide secure and reliable access to their compute resources. If this has a ring of familiarity, it is because President Trump earlier this year introduced a Ratepayer Protection Pledge , under which hyperscalers and AI companies agreed to protect US consumers from any bill shocks due to the energy and infrastructure requirements of their datacenter projects. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®

science.title: Who turned the W upside down? Why Cassiopeia won't sit still
science.description: null Some constellations are like old friends. You know them well, they're always there, and they never seem to change. A case in point is Cassiopeia, the queen. Its beautiful name comes from Greek mythology — the mother of Andromeda — and its shape is said to represent a queen sitting on a throne. To a stargazer, Cassiopeia is best known as a prominent northern constellation shaped like the letter W. It's easy to find — look north, find five reasonably bright stars making a W, congratulate yourself on finding Cassiopeia and use it to get somewhere more interesting. It's so often a signpost, not a destination. But look north a few hours after dark this month, and you'll notice the W has gone. The five stars are still there, but the shape you may have memorized looks like it's been picked up and turned over. It looks more like an E or an M, depending on when you look. Now try and look for the Big Dipper /the Plough. It's gone. Nothing mysterious has happened, of course. Cassiopeia is doing exactly what it always does, but it's a reminder that the northern sky is where you can easily watch the stars move — and the seasons turn. What's happening and when to look Stars move anti-clockwise around the north celestial pole, so Cassiopeia changes orientation. (Image credit: Alan Dyer/Stocktrek Images via Getty Images) Late November is an excellent time to reacquaint yourself with Cassiopeia from anywhere in the Northern Hemisphere. Look high in the northern sky during the evening for its five prominent stars — Caph, Schedar, Navi, Ruchbah and Segin. Depending on exactly when you look, it can look like a W, E, M or a 3. This is because Cassiopeia is circumpolar. Rather than rising in the east and eventually setting in the west like many familiar constellations , it circles the north celestial pole — a position currently held by Polaris , the North Star. From sufficiently northerly latitudes, its main stars never disappear below the horizon. This gives us a simple observing experiment. Find Cassiopeia in the early evening and remember its orientation relative to the horizon. Go back several hours later and look again. The constellation has moved around Polaris, and its shape has changed. The stars haven't changed their arrangement — Earth has simply rotated from west to east. We all know this logically, but watching the familiar pattern of Cassiopeia's stars apparently tip over during a single night makes Earth's rotation a lot less abstract. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 27, 1885: Astronomer captures 1st known photo of a meteor during an Andromedid meteor storm
science.description: null On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor. The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic. The meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower . The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet , which broke apart in the 1850s. When Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm . This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour. The November 1872 incidence of the Andromedid meteor shower, as seen over France, in a painting. (Image credit: Alto Vintage Images/Alamy) Why it mattered Not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible. But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name). Meteor Shower Quiz: How Well Do You Know 'Shooting Stars'? This modern photo of the Geminid meteor shower shows dozens of meteors captured in a long exposure by Josh Drury. Ladislaus Weinek, who captured the first photo of a meteor, had to use a photographic plate in 1889. (Image credit: Josh Dury) Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors. In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023. Want more space history? science.title: Astronomers watch a red giant star greedily devour a stellar 'Bao bun' before erupting: 'We couldn't quite believe our luck'
science.description: null Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER). "The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events." Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy , a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion. Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years, They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. They linked this to a star called WNTR23bzdiq / WTP19aalzlk that had been observed steadily brightening since 2019 after being stable for the preceding 30 years. Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. The team theorizes that Big Bao, with a mass seven times greater than the sun, expanded so rapidly and violently that it swallowed its smaller companion star. The unfortunate star, Little Bao, then spiraled into Big Bao's core in fewer than 10 orbits. "A couple of years back, we discovered a star that was gradually brightening. science.title: New Scientist Book Club: How urine changed the course of human history
science.description: A detail from Joseph Wright’s 1771 painting The Alchemist Discovering Phosphorus, showing Henning Brand in 1669 Science History Images/Alamy Imagine you could boil the development of science down to a single ingredient. A magical, mystical compound that transformed human history. Of course, science doesn’t work that way; even if breakthroughs shift the paradigm of our understanding, discovery doesn’t progress like a tech tree in a computer game, but as an interweaving tapestry of complementary and competing ideas and experimentation. Theories can bubble under the surface for centuries, overlooked because of politics or failure to realise their implications, while innovations can emerge from taking an idea in one industry and transplanting it to another. But, for a moment, try and picture what just one such ingredient could be. What would you pick? For centuries, in medieval Europe, alchemists quested for the “Philosopher’s Stone” that would finally help them achieve their dreams of transmutation. It was a search doomed to failure from the very beginning. And yet, a far better idea was under their noses – or, rather, their underpants – the entire time. My pick? Urine has a strong case for being the most transformative substance in human history. Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter The development of civilisation was built on chemistry. It required the first chemical reaction we mastered – fire – to keep us warm, cook our food and smelt ores. But leatherwork played an equally key role. Urine is a source of urea, which bacteria can break down into ammonia, granting early humans easy access to a base that could soften organic matter and tan hides. Across the world, leatherwork became the cornerstone of survival for every civilisation, from the Americas to Europe, Africa and Asia: even cultures that didn’t develop a bronze age, such as the Aztec, or skipped it entirely, as seen in Sub-Saharan Africa, relied on leatherwork for clothes, structures, industry and commerce. In ancient Rome, urine was so useful for laundries to keep togas whiter-than-white that Emperor Vespasian levied a tax on draining urinals. When his son complained, Vespasian’s response was blunt: pecunia non olet , money doesn’t stink. Part of the funds were used to build the Colosseum in Rome, today recognised as one of the wonders of the world. The magic of urine filtered into what would become chemical science, too. In the Leiden Papyrus X , part of a cluster of the only original manuscripts on alchemy’s origins we still have, you can find a recipe for faking gold using polysulfides. Place them in a vessel containing strong vinegar or the urine of a small child. Heat it from below, until the liquid appears like blood. Advertisement Decant this properly, and use. ” Unknown, Leiden Papyrus X , c. 300 CE In 1827, amid the dark, silent balm of an Egyptian night, a graverobber pulled a treasure from the sands. At first, the raider was frustrated; scavenging the tombs near Thebes, he had hoped to uncover a priceless heirloom, or a nugget of gold that would sparkle with lustre in the starlight. Instead, he had found only a clutch of rolled scrolls, made of papyrus and sealed against the elements. For a moment, he considered casting the documents aside and leaving them for the desert. Then greed got the better of him. Westerners loved all things Egyptian, he reasoned. Since the French had arrived with Napoleon, the new field of “Egyptology” had swept the continent, capturing the imagination of scholars and the wealthy. It was almost as popular as the new science of “chemistry”. Surely, if he took his find to the market, he’d find some gullible fool willing to buy it. The buyer’s name was Jean d’Anastasy, and he was anything but a fool. science.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
science.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
science.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Rocket Lab launches Japanese satellite into orbit in record-setting Thanksgiving Day liftoff (video)
science.description: null Rocket Lab added another satellite to a growing Japanese Earth-observation constellation on Thanksgiving Day (Nov. 26) in a record-setting liftoff for the company. An Electron rocket carrying a radar imaging satellite for Tokyo-based Earth-observation company Synspective is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab 's New Zealand launch site Thursday, during a window that opened 7 p.m. ET (0000 GMT/1 p.m. on Nov. 27 in New Zealand). It was the 22nd launch of the year for Rocket Lab, a new high record. "We set the pace, and then we break our own records," Rocket Lab said in an update on social media . It was the 101st launch overall for the company. You can see the mission, called "Night Owls Never Sleep," via Rocket Lab in the YouTube video at the top of this page. A Rocket Lab Electron rocket launches the Japanese radar satellite for the company Synspective's Strix imaging constellation on Nov. 26, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) We set the pace, and then we break our own records. "Night Owls Never Sleep" was our 22nd launch of the year - a new annual launch record for Electron. https://t.co/pzckdctiOE November 27, 2026 Synspective is building a network of "Strix" spacecraft equipped with synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which uses radio waves to generate detailed images of Earth's surface in both day and night lighting, as well as through cloud cover. Thursday's launch will be Rocket Lab's 14th for Synspective to date, and there are a lot more coming. At the end of September, Rocket Lab announced a deal with the company for an additional 20 Electron missions between 2028 and 2031 — the largest commercial launch contract in the rocket's history. That agreement brought Synspective's total number of contracted Electron flights to 47. Synspective aims to eventually establish a constellation capable of imaging locations anywhere on Earth at intervals of just a few hours. After its successful launch, the Electron's kick stage deployed the Strix satellite into low Earth orbit , 569 kilometers (353.6 miles) above our planet. "Night Owl Never Sleeps" marked the 101st mission to date for Rocket Lab. Ninety-two of them have been orbital flights with Electron; the other nine have been missions with HASTE , a suborbital variant of Electron that allows customers to test sensors and other equipment in the hypersonic flight environment.
